definition: As said by someone; used in the phrase according to.
examples: According to the news, it will snow tonight.
According to my mom, I was a quiet baby.
Everything went according to plan.

spanish.definition: Como dice alguien; se usa en la frase according to.

definition: For a short time only.
examples: The store is temporarily closed.
We're temporarily living with my parents.
The road was temporarily blocked.

spanish.definition: Solo por un tiempo corto.

definition: To get something back.
examples: I went back to retrieve my bag.
The dog retrieved the ball.
Can you retrieve the deleted files?

spanish.definition: Volver a obtener algo.

definition: To change something completely.
examples: The new paint transformed the room.
Having a baby transforms your life.
The city has transformed in ten years.

spanish.definition: Cambiar algo por completo.

definition: Friendly treatment of guests.
examples: Thank you for your hospitality.
People here are known for their hospitality.
She works in the hospitality industry.

spanish.definition: Trato amistoso a los invitados.

definition: To think again about a decision.
examples: Please reconsider your decision.
He asked her to reconsider.
We're reconsidering our plans for the summer.

spanish.definition: Volver a pensar en una decisión.

definition: A paper signed by many people to ask for a change.
examples: Please sign our petition.
Thousands of people signed the petition.
They started a petition to save the park.

spanish.definition: Papel firmado por muchas personas para pedir un cambio.

definition: To make something less tight.
examples: He loosened his tie.
Can you loosen this lid?
She's loosening the screws.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo menos apretado.

definition: The act of taking part in something.
examples: He denied any involvement in the crime.
Parent involvement helps kids in school.
Her involvement in the project ended last year.

spanish.definition: Acto de tomar parte en algo.

definition: The working parts of a machine; a way of doing something.
examples: The lock has a simple mechanism.
The clock's mechanism is broken.
We need a better mechanism for sharing information.

spanish.definition: Partes que funcionan en una máquina; manera de hacer algo.

definition: To get something, often with effort.
examples: You must obtain a permit first.
Where did you obtain this information?
She obtained a visa in two weeks.

spanish.definition: Conseguir algo, a menudo con esfuerzo.

definition: A very large, strong African ape.
examples: The gorilla sat in the shade.
We saw a baby gorilla at the zoo.
Gorillas live in family groups.

spanish.definition: Simio africano muy grande y fuerte.

definition: To act in a playful way to show you like someone.
examples: He likes to flirt with the waitress.
Are you flirting with me?
She smiled and flirted with him all night.

spanish.definition: Actuar de forma juguetona para mostrar que alguien te gusta.

definition: A character with special powers who helps people.
examples: My son wants to be a superhero.
Superman is a famous superhero.
She loves superhero movies.

spanish.definition: Personaje con poderes especiales que ayuda a la gente.

definition: A unit for measuring liquid, about half a liter.
examples: I bought a pint of ice cream.
He drank a pint of milk.
Add a pint of cream to the soup.

spanish.definition: Unidad para medir líquidos, cerca de medio litro.

definition: Connected to relations between countries; careful not to upset people.
examples: The two countries have good diplomatic relations.
She gave a very diplomatic answer.
He's traveling on a diplomatic passport.

spanish.definition: Relacionado con las relaciones entre países; cuidadoso de no molestar a la gente.

definition: The situation or words around something that help explain it.
examples: You can guess the word from the context.
He took my words out of context.
We need to look at this in context.

spanish.definition: Situación o palabras alrededor de algo que ayudan a explicarlo.

definition: To make something stronger or better; something that helps.
examples: Exercise can boost your mood.
The ad boosted our sales.
The win gave the team a real boost.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más fuerte o mejor; algo que ayuda.

definition: Not complete.
examples: We only got a partial refund.
The plan was a partial success.
He has partial hearing in one ear.

spanish.definition: Que no está completo.

definition: Something or someone that annoys you.
examples: These flies are a real nuisance.
Sorry to be a nuisance.
The noise is a nuisance to the neighbors.

spanish.definition: Algo o alguien que te molesta.

definition: The use of violence against people for political reasons.
examples: The world must fight terrorism.
He was arrested for terrorism.
The country suffered many years of terrorism.

spanish.definition: Uso de la violencia contra la gente por razones políticas.

definition: Not showing thanks for what you get.
examples: Don't be so ungrateful.
She felt her kids were ungrateful.
What an ungrateful man!

spanish.definition: Que no da las gracias por lo que recibe.

definition: To give money or things to help people.
examples: I donate blood twice a year.
They donated their old clothes.
She's donating $100 to the school.

spanish.definition: Dar dinero o cosas para ayudar a la gente.

definition: To make pain or worry less.
examples: This medicine will relieve the pain.
A hot bath relieves my stress.
I was relieved to hear the news.

spanish.definition: Reducir el dolor o la preocupación.

definition: Connected to a president.
examples: The presidential election is in November.
She watched the presidential debate.
He's a presidential candidate.

spanish.definition: Relacionado con un presidente.

definition: In a way that you did not expect.
examples: The test was surprisingly easy.
Surprisingly, nobody complained.
The food here is surprisingly good.

spanish.definition: De una manera que no esperabas.

definition: By itself, without a person controlling it.
examples: The door opens automatically.
The lights turn off automatically.
Your phone updates automatically at night.

spanish.definition: Por sí solo, sin que una persona lo controle.

definition: A college building where students live.
examples: She lives in a dorm on campus.
My dorm room is very small.
He met his best friend in the dorm.

spanish.definition: Edificio de universidad donde viven los estudiantes.

definition: Not liking change; a person with traditional ideas.
examples: My parents are very conservative.
He wore a conservative gray suit.
She's a conservative in politics.

spanish.definition: Que no le gustan los cambios; persona de ideas tradicionales.

definition: To refuse to think about something; to tell someone they can go.
examples: He dismissed the idea as silly.
The teacher dismissed the class early.
Don't dismiss her advice so quickly.

spanish.definition: Negarse a pensar en algo; decirle a alguien que se puede ir.

definition: The system of owning people and forcing them to work.
examples: Slavery ended in the US in 1865.
We studied the history of slavery.
Millions of people were sold into slavery.

spanish.definition: Sistema de ser dueño de personas y obligarlas a trabajar.

definition: Going in the same direction and always the same distance apart.
examples: The two streets are parallel.
Draw two parallel lines.
There's a clear parallel between the two stories.

spanish.definition: Que va en la misma dirección y siempre a la misma distancia.

definition: News reports about something; protection from insurance; phone signal.
examples: The election got a lot of TV coverage.
Does your plan include dental coverage?
There's no phone coverage in these mountains.

spanish.definition: Noticias sobre algo; protección de un seguro; señal de teléfono.

definition: A large stone building with a square base and a point on top.
examples: We visited the pyramids in Egypt.
The pyramid is thousands of years old.
She drew a pyramid on the board.

spanish.definition: Construcción grande de piedra con base cuadrada y una punta arriba.

definition: To build something again.
examples: They rebuilt the house after the fire.
It took years to rebuild the city.
We're rebuilding the old bridge.

spanish.definition: Volver a construir algo.

definition: A metal music instrument that you blow into.
examples: He plays the trumpet in a jazz band.
I could hear a trumpet in the street.
She's learning the trumpet at school.

spanish.definition: Instrumento musical de metal que se sopla.

definition: A gray powder used for building that gets hard when mixed with water.
examples: The workers mixed the cement.
The floor is made of cement.
Don't step on the wet cement.

spanish.definition: Polvo gris para construir que se endurece al mezclarlo con agua.

definition: Behavior that keeps bothering or threatening someone.
examples: She reported the harassment to her boss.
There are laws against harassment at work.
Online harassment is a serious problem.

spanish.definition: Comportamiento que sigue molestando o amenazando a alguien.

definition: A list of everything in a place; the goods a store has.
examples: We take inventory every January.
The store has too much inventory.
Make an inventory of everything in the house.

spanish.definition: Lista de todo lo que hay en un lugar; productos que tiene una tienda.

definition: Existing only in your mind.
examples: My daughter has an imaginary friend.
The story takes place in an imaginary city.
He's afraid of imaginary dangers.

spanish.definition: Que existe solo en tu mente.

definition: To move very fast; to make a picture look bigger or smaller.
examples: Cars zoomed past us.
Zoom in on the photo to see her face.
He zoomed down the hill on his bike.

spanish.definition: Moverse muy rápido; hacer que una imagen se vea más grande o más pequeña.

definition: A part of something; the amount of food for one person.
examples: The portions at this restaurant are huge.
A large portion of my pay goes to rent.
I ate only a small portion.

spanish.definition: Parte de algo; cantidad de comida para una persona.

definition: A situation that is strange because it is the opposite of what you expect.
examples: The irony is that the fire station burned down.
She said it with a hint of irony.
I love the irony of a dentist who eats candy all day.

spanish.definition: Situación extraña porque es lo contrario de lo que esperas.

definition: Much better than usual.
examples: She's an exceptional student.
The food was exceptional.
This is an exceptional opportunity.

spanish.definition: Mucho mejor de lo normal.

definition: A tube that makes faraway things look closer.
examples: We looked at the moon through a telescope.
He got a telescope for his birthday.
You can see Saturn with this telescope.

spanish.definition: Tubo que hace que las cosas lejanas se vean más cerca.

definition: A part of a song or a poem; a short part of the Bible.
examples: I only know the first verse of the song.
She read a verse from the Bible.
The poem has four verses.

spanish.definition: Parte de una canción o un poema; parte corta de la Biblia.

definition: A person who studies the mind and helps people with problems.
examples: She sees a psychologist once a week.
The school has a psychologist.
My brother is a child psychologist.

spanish.definition: Persona que estudia la mente y ayuda a la gente con sus problemas.

definition: A sudden wish to do something.
examples: I bought these shoes on impulse.
He felt an impulse to run away.
She fought the impulse to call him.

spanish.definition: Deseo repentino de hacer algo.

definition: A feeling of great shame in front of people.
examples: He couldn't stand the humiliation.
Losing so badly was a humiliation.
She suffered great humiliation at school.

spanish.definition: Sentimiento de gran vergüenza frente a la gente.

definition: Rude behavior toward someone.
examples: I meant no disrespect.
He showed disrespect to the teacher.
No disrespect, but I think you're wrong.

spanish.definition: Comportamiento grosero hacia alguien.

definition: A hard, smooth stone used in buildings; a small glass ball used in games.
examples: The kitchen has marble counters.
The floor is white marble.
The kids played marbles in the yard.

spanish.definition: Piedra dura y lisa usada en edificios; bola pequeña de vidrio para jugar.

definition: A work of art of the highest quality.
examples: The Mona Lisa is a masterpiece.
This movie is a true masterpiece.
She spent years painting her masterpiece.

spanish.definition: Obra de arte de la más alta calidad.

definition: A government, especially a strict one.
examples: The military regime fell in 1990.
Many people ran away from the regime.
The new regime closed the newspapers.

spanish.definition: Gobierno, sobre todo uno estricto.

definition: A group of things made or handled at one time.
examples: I baked a batch of cookies.
We got a new batch of students.
She made a big batch of soup.

spanish.definition: Grupo de cosas hechas o manejadas al mismo tiempo.

definition: To deal with a difficult problem; to knock a player down in a game.
examples: We need to tackle this problem now.
He tackled the player with the ball.
That was a hard tackle.

spanish.definition: Enfrentar un problema difícil; tumbar a un jugador en un juego.

definition: Not explained by science, like ghosts.
examples: Do you believe in supernatural powers?
The book is about supernatural events.
She says the house has a supernatural presence.

spanish.definition: Que la ciencia no explica, como los fantasmas.

definition: Having no money to pay what you owe.
examples: The company went bankrupt.
He was bankrupt at forty.
The medical bills left them bankrupt.

spanish.definition: Sin dinero para pagar lo que debes.

definition: Things that are sold in stores.
examples: The store has a lot of new merchandise.
Please don't touch the merchandise.
I bought some band merchandise at the concert.

spanish.definition: Cosas que se venden en las tiendas.

definition: Hard to walk on or hold because it is wet or smooth.
examples: Be careful, the floor is slippery.
The roads are slippery with ice.
Fish are slippery to hold.

spanish.definition: Difícil de pisar o agarrar por estar mojado o liso.

definition: A large area of sea partly surrounded by land.
examples: The storm moved into the Gulf of Mexico.
They sailed across the gulf.
The Gulf Coast has beautiful beaches.

spanish.definition: Área grande de mar rodeada en parte por tierra.

definition: A very quick look at something.
examples: I caught a glimpse of the singer.
We got a glimpse of the ocean from the train.
He had only a brief glimpse of the thief.

spanish.definition: Mirada muy rápida a algo.

definition: Money paid for loss, injury, or work.
examples: She got compensation for her injury.
The airline offered compensation for the delay.
The job has good compensation.

spanish.definition: Dinero que se paga por una pérdida, una lesión o un trabajo.

definition: To walk slowly and relax; a slow, relaxed walk.
examples: We strolled along the beach.
Let's take a stroll after dinner.
They were strolling through the park.

spanish.definition: Caminar despacio y relajado; caminata lenta y relajada.

definition: A place at a school or office where you get your own food.
examples: We eat lunch in the school cafeteria.
The hospital cafeteria is open all night.
The cafeteria food isn't very good.

spanish.definition: Lugar en una escuela u oficina donde tomas tu propia comida.

definition: Having a healthy mind; not crazy.
examples: No sane person would do that.
Running keeps me sane.
He's completely sane.

spanish.definition: Con la mente sana; que no está loco.

definition: The type of money used in a country.
examples: The euro is the currency of Spain.
Can I exchange currency at the airport?
What's the local currency in Brazil?

spanish.definition: Tipo de dinero que se usa en un país.

definition: To check that something is true.
examples: We need to verify your address.
Please verify your email.
The bank is verifying my information.

spanish.definition: Revisar que algo sea verdad.

definition: To look at something quickly; a quick look.
examples: Don't peek at your presents!
She peeked through the window.
Can I take a peek at your notes?

spanish.definition: Mirar algo rápido; mirada rápida.

definition: A pipe under the street that carries away dirty water.
examples: The sewer is blocked.
Rats live in the sewers.
The whole street smelled like a sewer.

spanish.definition: Tubo bajo la calle que se lleva el agua sucia.

definition: A very large deer with wide horns.
examples: We saw a moose in Canada.
A moose crossed the road in front of us.
Moose are bigger than horses.

spanish.definition: Venado muy grande con cuernos anchos.

definition: Something great that you did with effort.
examples: Finishing college was a big achievement.
This award is for lifetime achievement.
Her greatest achievement was raising three kids.

spanish.definition: Algo grande que hiciste con esfuerzo.

definition: Not wanting to wait.
examples: Don't be so impatient.
The customers were getting impatient.
I'm impatient to see the results.

spanish.definition: Que no quiere esperar.

definition: A lack of knowledge.
examples: His ignorance surprised me.
Ignorance of the law is no excuse.
Hate often comes from ignorance.

spanish.definition: Falta de conocimiento.

definition: A person who makes something new.
examples: He's the creator of this TV show.
Walt Disney was the creator of Mickey Mouse.
She's a video creator on YouTube.

spanish.definition: Persona que hace algo nuevo.

definition: Full of energy; the way people act together.
examples: She's a very dynamic leader.
New York is a dynamic city.
The family dynamic changed after the divorce.

spanish.definition: Lleno de energía; manera en que la gente actúa junta.

definition: The act of giving or sending things to many people or places.
examples: The distribution of food began at noon.
He works in film distribution.
There's an unfair distribution of money.

spanish.definition: Acto de dar o enviar cosas a muchas personas o lugares.

definition: To pretend you will do something or know something.
examples: I think he's bluffing.
She bluffed her way through the interview.
Don't play cards with him; he bluffs very well.

spanish.definition: Fingir que vas a hacer algo o que sabes algo.

definition: Too painful or bad to accept.
examples: The heat was unbearable.
The pain became unbearable.
He's unbearable when he loses.

spanish.definition: Demasiado doloroso o malo para aceptarlo.

definition: Easy to see or understand.
examples: It soon became apparent that he was lying.
For no apparent reason, she started to cry.
The problem wasn't apparent at first.

spanish.definition: Fácil de ver o entender.

definition: Very serious and sad.
examples: The news looks grim.
He had a grim look on his face.
The future of the factory is grim.

spanish.definition: Muy serio y triste.

definition: From the time between about 500 and 1500.
examples: We visited a medieval castle.
She studies medieval history.
The town still has its medieval walls.

spanish.definition: De la época entre cerca de 500 y 1500.

definition: Refusing to accept that something is true.
examples: He's in denial about his drinking.
The company issued a denial.
She's in denial about the divorce.

spanish.definition: Negarse a aceptar que algo es verdad.

definition: A thin metal music instrument that you blow across.
examples: She plays the flute in the school band.
I heard a flute in the distance.
He's taking flute lessons.

spanish.definition: Instrumento musical delgado de metal que se sopla de lado.

definition: A short message at work.
examples: Did you read the memo from the boss?
She sent a memo to all the staff.
I never got that memo.

spanish.definition: Mensaje corto en el trabajo.

definition: A person who gives advice as a job.
examples: She's a financial advisor.
I talked to my college advisor.
He's a top advisor to the president.

spanish.definition: Persona cuyo trabajo es dar consejos.

definition: Too bad to be allowed.
examples: This behavior is unacceptable.
That's an unacceptable price.
Your work is unacceptable.

spanish.definition: Demasiado malo para permitirlo.

definition: Important in history.
examples: This is a historic moment.
We walked through the historic center of the city.
It was a historic win for the team.

spanish.definition: Importante en la historia.

definition: A large black and white bear from China.
examples: Pandas eat bamboo.
We saw a baby panda at the zoo.
The panda was sleeping in a tree.

spanish.definition: Oso grande blanco y negro de China.

definition: Giving help and kindness.
examples: My family is very supportive.
She has a supportive husband.
Thanks for being so supportive.

spanish.definition: Que da ayuda y amabilidad.

definition: A long piece of cloth with words on it.
examples: They hung a banner across the street.
The fans held up a banner.
They carried a banner in the parade.

spanish.definition: Pedazo largo de tela con palabras.

definition: Likely to change in ways you can't guess.
examples: The weather here is unpredictable.
He's a very unpredictable person.
The end of the game was unpredictable.

spanish.definition: Que puede cambiar de maneras que no puedes adivinar.

definition: A group of things of the same type.
examples: Which category does this book go in?
She won in the best actress category.
The website sorts products by category.

spanish.definition: Grupo de cosas del mismo tipo.

definition: To appear in a place as a ghost; to stay in your mind and worry you.
examples: They say a ghost haunts this house.
That memory still haunts me.
Her mistake came back to haunt her.

spanish.definition: Aparecer en un lugar como fantasma; quedarse en tu mente y preocuparte.

definition: To take something quickly and roughly.
examples: A thief snatched her bag.
He snatched the letter from my hand.
She's always snatching food off my plate.

spanish.definition: Quitar algo de forma rápida y brusca.

definition: From the hot parts of the world.
examples: We stayed on a tropical island.
Mango is a tropical fruit.
A tropical storm is coming.

spanish.definition: De las partes calientes del mundo.

definition: To breathe in through your nose, often to smell something.
examples: The dog sniffed my shoes.
She sniffed the milk to see if it was bad.
Stop sniffing and blow your nose.

spanish.definition: Tomar aire por la nariz, a menudo para oler algo.

definition: An important new discovery.
examples: Doctors made a breakthrough in cancer research.
This is a major breakthrough for our team.
We finally had a breakthrough in the case.

spanish.definition: Descubrimiento nuevo e importante.

definition: To eat a meal, especially dinner.
examples: We dined at a nice Italian restaurant.
They like to dine out on Fridays.
We were dining on the terrace.

spanish.definition: Comer una comida, sobre todo la cena.

definition: An arm or a leg; a large branch of a tree.
examples: He lost a limb in the war.
A tree limb fell on our car.
My limbs were sore after the race.

spanish.definition: Brazo o pierna; rama grande de un árbol.

definition: Unable to feel anything.
examples: My fingers are numb from the cold.
The dentist made my mouth numb.
She felt numb after the bad news.

spanish.definition: Que no puede sentir nada.
